questions.question: Describe hieroglyphics and how they were read again.
questions.expected_answer: Hieroglyphics was ancient Egyptian picture-writing, with more than seven hundred signs; some stood for sounds and others for words or ideas. It could be written in rows or columns, read towards the faces of people and animals, and royal names were in cartouches. The Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, had the same message in hieroglyphics and Greek, and Champollion used it to read hieroglyphics in 1822.

questions.question: Explain how the Egyptians used mathematics.
questions.expected_answer: They counted in tens, with signs such as a stroke for one, a heel bone for ten, a coil of rope for a hundred and a lotus for a thousand, but no zero. They added, subtracted, multiplied, divided and used fractions. They measured in cubits, re-measured fields with ropes after each flood, which helped develop geometry, and planned the pyramids carefully.

questions.question: How did the Egyptians use the stars to make a calendar?
questions.expected_answer: They noticed that Sirius reappeared before sunrise just before the Nile flood began, so they made that the start of the new year. Their calendar had 365 days: twelve months of thirty days plus five extra days. They divided night and day into twelve hours each, using stars, sundials and water clocks, which gave us our twenty-four hours.
